Q: Portably disabling FMA for a single function A:

Some pragmas can be put inside functions, is it the case for this one? You can store to a volatile variable (or use a pass-through like asm ("" : "+x"(x))) to block optimizations. This won't be enough to make the code really robust anyway.

Q: Is it normal that std::unorder_map has different bucket_counts? A:

Yes, this is normal. Try to implement a bucket-based map from scratch, and you will see that there is some degree of arbitrariness in the way the set of keys is broken into buckets. This classification is based on the value of the hash code obtained from every key. Every time you get a new key and its hash code, you have to decide if you have to create a new bucket or add this key to an existing bucket closest by the hash code value. Note that at the moment of this decision, you don't know the total number of key-value pairs in the map during its lifetime. This decision is a matter of optimization, so you have a trade-off between the complexity of this calculation and the optimization of the set of buckets.

I am not sure if you put any difference in your sample compared to the sample on this page, but the number of buckets can be implementation-dependent. Note the word possible in possible output.

Q: How can I query a value in SQL Server XML column A:

In case you want to find other node besides "Alpha", the query should be something like this:

select Roles from MyTable where Roles.exist('(/*:root/*:role[contains(.,"Beta")])') = 1

Q: uninstall openjdk in mac A:

A JDK can be installed anywhere on your Mac, not just /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines.

If you ask IntelliJ to install a JDK for you, it goes into your_home_folder/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines. If you use SDKMAN! to install JDKs, they land in your_home_folder/.sdkman/candidates/.

which java

In Terminal.app (or any such console), type and execute:

which java

You will see the path to the java executable.

Tip: I find the easiest way to locate, download, install, uninstall, and set default JDK is with SDKMAN!.

Q: “Unable to find manifest signing certificate in the certificate store” - even when add new key A:

Assuming this is a personal certificate created by windows on the system you copied your project from, you can use the certificate manager on the system where the project is now and import the certificate:

  • Start the certificate manager (certmgr).
  • Select the Personal > Certificates.
  • Right click below the list of existing certificates.
  • Select "Import..." from the All Tasks context menu.
  • Use the browse button to find the .pfx in the project (the .pfx from the previous system that you copied over with the project). It should be in the sub-directory with the same name as the project directory.

I am familiar with C# and VS, so if that is not your environment maybe the .pfx will be elsewhere or maybe this suggestion does not apply. After the import you should get a status message. If you succeeded, the compile certificate error should be gone.

Q: Where does IntelliJ store the JDKs that it downloads on my behalf? A:

tl;dr

/Users/your_username_here/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/

Choose File > Project Structure > Platform Settings > SDKs

You can inspect the JDKs known to IntelliJ by choosing File > Project Structure > Platform Settings > SDKs.

Notice how the location of the selected JDK is shown in the JDK home path field.

In this example, the JDK downloaded by IntelliJ was put in:

/Users/your_username_here/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/

Note that this location contrasts with the location used by some of the independent JDK installers. In my experience, those tools use the root /Library path (system-wide, all users), rather than in the particular user’s ~/Library. That full path would be: /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines.

SDKMAN!

By the way, an alternative tool I prefer for finding, downloading, installing, and uninstalling JDKs (and other software kits like Gradle) is SDKMAN!. It is a command-line tool for Unix-like operating systems including macOS.

SDKMAN! stores the JDKs in your_home_folder/.sdkman/candidates/.
